recommendation.rationale: Fleischner recommends, for a solitary, pure ground-glass/non-solid, incidental pulmonary nodule 6mm or greater in diameter, in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised: a CT at 6-12 months to confirm persistence, and, only if the nodule is confirmed persistent, continued CT surveillance every 2 years until 5 years. The Local SOP's own wording states this boundary as '>6mm'; the governed executable boundary is '>=6mm', per explicit clinical HITL approval treating the Local SOP wording as an imprecise transcription of the underlying Fleischner 2017 source table (see clinical/sources/local-sop.json findings).

recommendation.rationale: Fleischner recommends no routine follow-up for a solitary, part-solid, incidental pulmonary nodule less than 6mm in whole-nodule diameter, in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised. recommendation.rationale: Fleischner recommends, for a solitary, part-solid, incidental pulmonary nodule with whole-nodule diameter >=6mm and a solid component <6mm in diameter, in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised: a CT at 3-6 months to confirm persistence, and, only if the nodule is confirmed persistent, continued annual CT surveillance through 5 years. The Local SOP's own wording states only a simplified whole-nodule <6/>6mm trajectory with no solid-component distinction; the >=6mm boundary and the solid-component <6mm stratification are primary-Fleischner clarifications materially beyond the Local SOP text (see provenance anchors). A whole-nodule >=6mm nodule with a solid component >=6mm is a different, more suspicious Fleischner state and is explicitly out of scope for this rule.

recommendation.rationale: Fleischner recommends, for a solitary, part-solid, incidental pulmonary nodule with a solid component greater than 8mm in diameter, in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised: further characterization by PET/CT, or biopsy/tissue sampling, or resection -- presented as coequal options with no source-stated ranking or timing between them. Recommendation 4 states no independent whole-nodule diameter threshold for this trigger; the whole-nodule diameter is not evaluated by this rule. This content is materially absent from the Local SOP text, which contains no escalation/PET-CT/biopsy content for part-solid nodules at all -- this rule's entire clinical basis is the primary Fleischner guideline.

recommendation.rationale: S3 states that a solitary, solid, incidental pulmonary nodule under CT surveillance may be discharged from further routine follow-up once EITHER its volume increase over approximately one year is below the source's stated 25% threshold, OR its volume-doubling time exceeds 600 days, OR the patient's general condition does not permit further diagnostic clarification or therapy -- three independently sufficient discharge criteria from the same source sentence, in a patient >=18 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised. The general-condition criterion is recorded exclusively as an explicit clinician attestation of the S3 criterion itself, never derived from ECOG/performance status, age, comorbidity, life expectancy, operability, treatment candidacy, or any other input -- the source states no such decomposition, and none is invented here. The app does not calculate volume change, elapsed time, or VDT itself -- all three criteria are explicit clinician attestations/entries. A Local-SOP table elsewhere additionally conditions a >600-day VDT finding on 2-year radiological stability; that precondition is not part of the S3 narrative's own discharge sentence and is not applied here. None of the three criteria being met does not, by itself, imply growth or trigger any work-up recommendation in this Rule-Set Release.

recommendation.rationale: S3 states that, in the case of radiologically documented size progression of an isolated pulmonary nodule -- characterized by a volume-doubling time below 400 days -- definitive pathological clarification should be pursued, in a patient >=18 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised. VDT<400 is the guideline's own quantitative characterization of this progression criterion, not a second, independently required progression finding. The primary S3 guideline names three procedures for this confirmation -- bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy, CT-guided transthoracic biopsy, or minimally invasive surgical resection -- presented as coequal alternatives with no source-stated ranking or sequence between them; the source states the choice among them is made interdisciplinarily, involving pulmonology, radiology, and thoracic surgery, and this app does not select a procedure on its own. This branch does not use PET-CT, the Brock/Herder risk models, the >8mm initial-assessment pathway, any additional VDT threshold, or any minimum persistence duration -- none is stated by the source for this criterion. The app does not calculate VDT itself -- it is an explicit clinician entry. A same-source B1 discharge rule (ACR-S3-FOLLOWUP-DISCHARGE-VOLUME-OR-VDT) with unresolved status (s3_volume_stability_criterion_met absent) does not block this match, per the governed directional relation declared above (ADR-0011).
